title: Mathematics — notable papers in the Friday, 6 November 2026 announcement batch
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an inferred, result-driven selection rather than a measured popularity ranking. Attention evidence and citation data are limited for papers announced only days ago.

sections.title: Tusnády's problem and online two-sample thinning
sections.abstract: The author proves the sharp discrepancy order in Tusnády's problem in every fixed dimension, a robust lower bound after limited deletions, and minimax rates for online thinning of two samples, including a sharp one-dimensional terminal rate.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 gives Δ_d(N)=Θ_d((log N)^(d−1/2)) for fixed d≥2; Theorem 1.2 gives minimax expected prefix discrepancy Θ_{k,ρ}((log n)^(k+1/2)) for fixed k≥1 and 0<ρ<2. For k=1, terminal discrepancy is Θ_ρ((log log n)^(3/2)).
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Geometry result for worst-case finite point sets and axis-parallel boxes. Thinning uses two independent size-n samples from an unknown common Borel law; decisions are online and irrevocable with expected deletion budget ρn.
sections.unique_caveat: For k≥2, terminal-thinning upper and lower bounds remain separated by a factor of log n; the sharp prefix rate does not close this gap.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Independent same-batch proof of the sharp Tusnády order for d≥2 plus quantitative online-thinning results; the paper identifies a remaining terminal gap. No citation momentum was used.

sections.title: Resolving Tusnády's Problem
sections.abstract: The author proves a matching lower bound for combinatorial discrepancy of anchored boxes in each fixed dimension at least three; combined with existing bounds, this determines the order for axis-parallel boxes in every fixed dimension at least two.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 gives discrepancy at least c_d(log N)^(d−1/2) for anchored boxes for each fixed d≥3; with known upper bounds and the planar result, the authors derive Θ_d((log N)^(d−1/2)) for axis-parallel boxes for all fixed d≥2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: N-point sets, axis-parallel or anchored boxes, and fixed dimension; constants may depend on dimension.
sections.unique_caveat: Dimension-dependent constants are not optimized. The new lower-bound proof treats d≥3; the planar lower bound for the all-dimensions conclusion is prior work.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The main theorem closes the remaining logarithmic-factor gap for fixed d≥3 and independently corroborates the sharp-order result in paper 1; the proof arguments differ.

sections.title: First-Order Model Checking on Monadically Dependent Graph Classes
sections.abstract: The authors prove fixed-parameter tractability of first-order model checking on every monadically dependent graph class and, with the known hardness direction, give the conjectured characterization for hereditary classes.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 gives an algorithm running in O_{C,φ,ε}(n^(3+ε)) on n-vertex graphs in a monadically dependent class C; Theorem 1.2 bounds the number of fixed-rank types over a finite parameter set polynomially in its size.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: First-order model checking on graphs in a monadically dependent class; the running-time guarantee depends on the class, formula, and ε. The full hereditary-class characterization also uses the previously established hardness direction and FPT ≠ AW[*].
sections.unique_caveat: The tractability theorem applies when the input graph belongs to a monadically dependent class, and the stated exponent is 3+ε, not a uniform cubic bound.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract identifies resolution of the tractability direction of a central model-checking conjecture. The paper links a Lean formalization and combines graph structure, locality, and type counting.

sections.title: An extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37
sections.abstract: The author constructs an extremal unimodular lattice of rank 37 and minimum four, resolving the last undetermined optimal minimum through rank 48; an explicit 4-frame also yields a length-37 self-dual code.
sections.claimed_result: The main theorem constructs an integral unimodular lattice of rank 37 and minimum four, with automorphism group AGL(1,13)×C6; an explicit 4-frame yields a Type I self-dual Z/4Z code of length 37 and minimum Euclidean weight 16.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Positive-definite integral unimodular lattices; minimum is the smallest squared norm of a nonzero lattice vector. The code conclusion uses a 4-frame.
sections.unique_caveat: The result settles rank 37, not higher ranks; the code conclusion depends on the explicit 4-frame supplied in the paper.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The introduction identifies rank 37 as the last unresolved optimal-minimum case through rank 48; the construction also settles the corresponding length-37 code case.

sections.title: Pointless K3 surfaces over finite fields
sections.abstract: The authors prove that K3 surfaces without rational points over the finite field with q elements exist if and only if q≤11, using lattice bounds, the Artin–Tate formula, and Niemeier-lattice embeddings.
sections.claimed_result: A K3 surface with no F_q-rational point exists exactly when the prime power q≤11; the authors note an improved bound for certain threefold rational-point results.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Smooth K3 surfaces over finite fields, with q a prime power; the classification concerns existence of a rational point over the field of definition.
sections.unique_caveat: Specific to K3 surfaces over finite fields. The authors mention an independent proof and a relationship between two lattice/Frobenius viewpoints they have not worked out.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A sharp existence/nonexistence cutoff in arithmetic geometry with a proof route linking finite-field point counts and definite lattices; the authors note an independent proof.

sections.title: The probabilistic bound for perfect hashing is sharp only for binary alphabets
sections.abstract: For perfect q-hash codes, the authors prove that the classical probabilistic rate lower bound is attained only at q=2, give a strict improvement for q≥3, and establish a larger asymptotic improvement for sufficiently large q.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show R_q=B_q iff q=2 and, for every η>0, R_q≥B_q+exp(-(2+η)q) for all sufficiently large q; they bound what subexponential-length pairwise-uniform inner codes can achieve within the studied concatenation framework.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Asymptotic rate R_q of perfect q-hash codes as block length tends to infinity for integer alphabet size q; the exponential-scale theorem has an unspecified threshold q_0(η).
sections.unique_caveat: These are lower bounds, not an exact determination of R_q; the exact exponential order of R_q−B_q remains undetermined.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Proves the first assertion of the Xing–Yuan conjecture for every q≥3 and improves the known asymptotic scale of the excess lower bound; cross-listed in information theory.

sections.title: On do Carmo's Question: The Properly Embedded Case
sections.abstract: The author proves every complete noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded constant-mean-curvature hypersurface of finite Morse index in Euclidean space is minimal, in every dimension, without curvature or volume-growth bounds.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1 states that a smooth, connected, complete, noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded, boundaryless CMC hypersurface of finite Morse index in R^(n+1) has zero mean curvature for every n≥2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Complete, noncompact, two-sided, properly embedded, boundaryless, finite-index hypersurface in Euclidean space; proof uses an inscribed-radius weight and stability outside a compact set.
sections.unique_caveat: Proper embeddedness is essential to the presented proof; the result does not cover arbitrary immersed hypersurfaces in every dimension.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Removes dimension restrictions and curvature/volume-growth bounds for the properly embedded finite-index case; the introduction contrasts this with prior bounded-curvature or limited-dimension results.

sections.title: Weak uniqueness for the stochastic heat equation with nondegenerate diffusion: the full Hölder regime
sections.abstract: The author proves weak well-posedness for the scalar stochastic heat equation on the one-dimensional torus with uniformly nondegenerate diffusion Hölder continuous at every positive order, extending an earlier result above exponent 2/3.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 gives weak existence and uniqueness in law for bounded, uniformly nondegenerate, positively Hölder diffusion and deterministic L² initial data. Theorem 1.2 extends to measurable drifts of linear growth and allows unbounded diffusion under a separate initial-data condition.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: One-dimensional torus, scalar stochastic heat equation. Theorem 1.1 assumes bounded, uniformly nondegenerate, β-Hölder diffusion for β>0; the unbounded-diffusion extension in Theorem 1.2 assumes bounded initial data.
sections.unique_caveat: This is weak well-posedness (uniqueness in law), not pathwise uniqueness. The authors suggest the L∞ initial-data assumption in the unbounded-diffusion case might be reduced to L² with a finer argument.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Claims the full positive-Hölder range left open by an earlier result and states separate theorems for bounded and unbounded diffusion; a focused stochastic-analysis result.

sections.title: An Accelerated Proximal Gradient Method for Bures-Wasserstein Space
sections.abstract: The authors lift a class of composite optimization problems on Gaussian measures in Bures–Wasserstein space to affine transport maps and obtain an accelerated method with an O(k^-2) objective gap, including a faster rate for a specified Gaussian variational-inference setting.
sections.claimed_result: BW-FISTA achieves objective gap O(k^-2) when objective components admit the required convex smooth and convex proximable affine lifts; for log-concave, log-smooth Gaussian variational inference, an entropy term admits an exact proximal step.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Optimization over Bures–Wasserstein space of Gaussian measures with the stated affine-lift regularity; the variational-inference result assumes a log-concave, log-smooth target and the paper's stochastic-gradient noise conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: The rate guarantee applies to the specified liftable objective class; numerical experiments do not establish performance beyond that setting.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a minimax-optimal O(k^-2) rate and an improvement from O(k^-1) for its Gaussian variational-inference application; the listing reports NeurIPS 2026 workshop acceptance.

sections.title: An improved minimum degree threshold for fractional clique decompositions in partite graphs
sections.abstract: The authors prove a Dirac-type minimum-degree condition sufficient for fractional K_r-decompositions of large balanced r-partite graphs, yielding an asymptotic threshold bound for ordinary clique decompositions.
sections.claimed_result: For sufficiently large r-partite graphs with n vertices in each part and partite minimum degree at least (1−1/(30r²))n, the authors prove a fractional K_r-decomposition, subject to necessary divisibility conditions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Balanced r-partite graphs, sufficiently large part size, and divisibility conditions; the stated consequence is an asymptotic upper bound on the minimum-degree threshold for a K_r-decomposition.
sections.unique_caveat: The condition is sufficient and asymptotic; it does not identify the exact threshold for each finite graph size.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract gives a concrete improved degree threshold and reduction from fractional to ordinary clique decompositions; no cross-list or citation signal was used.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
text: Two independent papers, Lei and Wengiel, claim the sharp fixed-dimensional Tusnády order. Both use Gaussian small-ball ideas in lower bounds, but Lei adds robust deletion and online thinning; these two papers do not imply an archive-wide shift.

Kubischta's rank-37 lattice construction settles an extremal unimodular-lattice case and yields a self-dual code; Auel, Engel, Kedlaya, and Shaikh use lattice bounds and Niemeier embeddings for K3 point classification. These separate results share lattice structure as a bridge between existence and classification.
Perfect hashing and fractional clique decomposition sharpen distinct combinatorial bounds by different methods.
Model checking is a focused logic/structural graph theory result; CMC geometry, stochastic PDE, and Bures–Wasserstein optimization are distinct isolated advances, not a shared method trend.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
text: Author-stated gap: Lei leaves terminal-thinning bounds for k≥2 separated by log n; close the gap under online irrevocable decisions and the stated deletion budget.
Author-stated limitation: Wengiel does not optimize dimension-dependent constants or thresholds; seek explicit dependence or sharper finite-N bounds.
Author-identified connection: the K3 paper notes but does not work out the relationship between its Artin–Tate approach and the independent proof's Frobenius/lattice perspective.

Author-stated scope gap: Niu says proper embeddedness is essential to the proof; constructing a suitable weight for general complete immersed CMC hypersurfaces could advance the broader finite-index question.
Author-stated extension: Han suggests the L∞ initial-data condition for unbounded diffusion may be reducible to L² with a finer near-time-zero argument.
Result gap: Li and Shi do not determine R_q; refining the exponential order of R_q−B_q and studying constructions beyond the analyzed concatenation framework are proposed directions.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.text: The clearest headline is the pair of independent Tusnády results, with the online-thinning paper adding a second minimax problem and a precise unresolved terminal gap. Elsewhere, papers close specific cases in model checking, unimodular lattices, and K3 arithmetic geometry. This is theorem- and corroboration-driven ordering, not measured readership; the preprints' claims still merit expert review.

sections.title: Method and sources
sections.text: Daily window 2026-11-06 through 2026-11-06; latest Mathematics announcement batch on 2026-11-09 was Friday 2026-11-06, prior to snapshot 2026-11-09T01:24:56Z. Traversed the full 409-entry arXiv Mathematics batch; ten selected papers were deduplicated by versionless arXiv ID and checked against arXiv metadata and abstract pages. Introductions and main results for the top three were inspected. Ordering is inferred from theorem-level results, cross-listing, independent same-result work, and venue/proof-artifact signals. Semantic Scholar citation metadata could not be obtained for this snapshot, so no citation counts or momentum ranking are claimed; arXiv provides no official trending chart.
